name: heather

attributes.attribute: tough low-growing bog plant with pink or purplish flowers
bees make a favorite honey from it in parts of Scotland
classed as a peasant tree in Ireland yet included in the tree alphabet
symbol of the wild open moors of the Celtic world

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Heather is a symbolic plant, common in Ireland and Britain. The low-growing heath is a tough bog plant. It blooms with pink or purplish flowers that carpet wild areas in summer. Bees love heather and make from it a honey that is a favorite food in parts of Scotland. In Ireland people classed heather as a peasant tree. Even so, it appears in the tree alphabet. Heather marked the moors and stood for the wild open land of the Celtic world.
objective: Document heather, the symbolic moor plant of the Celts.
key_results: Record its growth and summer bloom.
Describe its place as a peasant plant in the tree alphabet.
evidence: Monaghan, P. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore (2008): heather entry.
